description: Lottery group of voice IDs used when a game event should randomly choose one of several spoken lines.

Id.technical: FName primary key. IDs come from CharacterVoiceGroup.Id_VoiceGroup, ShikigamiVoiceGroup.Id_VoiceGroup, CharacterSound.Id_VoiceGroup, mission-task voice text arrays, sequencer section IDs and explicit CP call literals. The typed finder walks DTM.VoiceGroupDataTables (+0x750), rejects None when requested, and returns the first row with this Id. Export spells it ID.

Id_Voice.simple: Voice IDs in the random-pick pool.
Id_Voice.technical: TArray<FName>, parallel to no weight array. Consumers filter None entries and pick by weighted index, random stream, or shuffle, depending on subsystem: sound voice player gives each non-None entry weight 1; battle task voices shuffle non-None candidates while excluding a specified entry and optionally the last played line; CP_240 and the unique-pair evaluator remove the previously picked voice when at least two candidates remain. Every chosen ID is then resolved against VoiceDataTable.

notes: Loaded as a DataTable primary asset named VoiceGroupDataTable into DTM.VoiceGroupDataTables (+0x750).
This is the second layer of the usual voice join: action/system data selects a VoiceGroup row, and this array selects one VoiceDataTable row to play.

None placeholders are common and are generally filtered. The shikigami consumer counts non-None entries but then indexes the original array with the fraction of that count, so a None entry in the middle could still be selected; this is an observed implementation quirk, not a data rule.
The companion export is partial; no claim is made about all retail rows or Blueprint-only references. Source is reconstructed retail C++ with retail RVAs recorded inline.

usages.detail: Shared typed voice-group row finder used by action voice playback.
Action controller resolves the group selected by CharacterVoiceGroup.
CharacterSound voice group path uses a uniform lottery over non-None entries.
Battle task voice shuffles candidates and avoids immediate repeats.
CP_240 removes the last picked variant before random selection.
Unique-pair common fallback collects non-None group voices.
